headline: AFP Rejects Chinese Claims, Says Philippines Will Not Abandon BRP Sierra Madre
seoTitle: AFP Rejects China Claims on BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin | FMB News
seoDescription: The AFP rejected Chinese Embassy claims concerning the BRP Sierra Madre and reaffirmed the Philippines' intention to maintain its presence at Ayungin Shoal.
deck: The military rejected the Chinese Embassy's latest claims and said the Philippines has no plan to abandon the grounded Navy vessel that serves as its outpost at Ayungin Shoal.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Armed Forces of the Philippines on Sunday rejected claims from the Chinese Embassy concerning the BRP Sierra Madre and said the Philippines has no plan to abandon the grounded Navy vessel at Ayungin Shoal.

AFP West Philippine Sea spokesperson retired Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad said the military would continue supporting personnel stationed aboard the ship and maintaining the country's presence at the shoal.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The BRP Sierra Madre has served as a Philippine military outpost at Ayungin Shoal since 1999. Rotation and resupply missions to the vessel have repeatedly become flashpoints in the broader Philippines-China dispute in the West Philippine Sea.

The Philippines cites the 2016 South China Sea arbitral award and its rights within its exclusive economic zone. China rejects that award and maintains competing claims. Those legal and diplomatic positions remain contested between the two governments.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The condition and continued operation of the Sierra Madre are central to the Philippines' physical presence at Ayungin Shoal. Statements about its maintenance, resupply or possible removal therefore carry immediate security and diplomatic significance.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Attention will remain on future rotation and resupply missions, diplomatic exchanges between Manila and Beijing, and whether the provisional understanding governing those missions continues to reduce confrontation at sea.
